Asha: seeing a strange p99 tail spike after the kernel selector rollout. p95 steady ~120ms but p99 jumped from ~260ms to ~480ms on small-batch prefill workloads. not sure if it's kernel selection or kv warmup :thinking:
Ryan: which kernel path did the selector pick? matmul_fast -> matmul_generic fallback?
Asha: selector logs show fast->generic for seq_len<=8 on A100 after the quantization tweak. it only triggers for small microbatches (<=4).
Toni: can you paste a short profiler run? a 30s capture with cpu+gpu timelines should show head-of-line stalls. e.g.:
```
./rprof run --duration 30s --trace cpu,gpu --filter "model:*/gpt*" --output /tmp/trace.pb
python tools/trace_viewer /tmp/trace.pb
```
Kevin: another thought — kv-cache cold misses can cascade during prefill. if a microbatch groups several cold prefixes, the prefill cost multiplies and blocks decode lanes. did we see kvcache-miss counters spike?
Asha: yes kvcache.miss_rate jumped ~4x in the same window. also noticed an increase in kernel alignment mismatches (padding after quant change). small batches + kvcache misses => longer prefill per-request.
Ryan: so two interacting issues: selector flips kernels causing slower matmul for tiny workloads, plus kv miss cascade increasing prefill time. both hit p99 but not p95 much. makes sense.
Toni: quick repro steps I ran locally that matched production:
```
# synthetic small-batch prefill-heavy load
python bench/sim_load.py --concurrency 16 --batch-size 2 --seq-len 6 --kv-cold-rate 0.7 --model gpt-small-quant
```
That reproduces p99 tail in ~90s.
Kevin: mitigation options (short term):
- raise selector threshold to prefer generic for seq <=8 on quantized models
- warm kvcache proactively for small prefixes (background prefetch)
- throttle microbatch grouping so prefill-heavy requests don't co-locate with decode-bound ones
Which should we prioritize?
Asha: my vote is selector tweak (fastest roll) + microbatching policy change. prefetching is higher risk (IO/cost).
Ryan: agree. also add perf counters to kernel-selection path so we can break down time spent in matmul vs kv handling in the trace. small patch suggestion:
```
diff --git a/selector/kernel_selector.cpp b/selector/kernel_selector.cpp
@@
- if (score_fast > score_generic) return FAST;
+ // prefer generic for tiny seqs on quantized paths; avoids alignment fallback penalty
+ if (seq_len <= 8 && model.is_quantized()) return GENERIC;
+ if (score_fast > score_generic) return FAST;
```
Toni: please run perf job with that patch in a canary fleet (10% traffic), check p99 delta, and also verify token-throughput doesn't regress.
deploy-bot: rolled selector v2.1.4-canary to fleet=eng-runtime-canary at 2026-03-18T14:02:10Z :rocket:
Asha: canary metrics show early win — p99 down ~120ms in the canary after 10m. still seeing occasional kv miss spikes.
Kevin: let's also add a microbatch policy flag: prefer_latency_sensitive=true which caps group_size to 3 for routes flagged as low-latency. low effort and reversible.
Ryan: I'll open an RFC with the exact scheduler change + tests.
Toni: i'll schedule a perf capture of the canary tomorrow morning and dump flamegraphs for the worst p99 traces.
Asha: thanks all. next actions: (1) Ryan RFC for scheduler, (2) canary perf capture + flamegraphs, (3) consider background kv prefetch if spikes persist.
Ryan: noted, will sync in 1:1 after RFC draft. :thumbsup:
